headline: DBM Earmarks ₱45.67 Billion for 2027 Disaster Fund as El Niño Risks Loom
seoTitle: DBM Sets ₱45.67B 2027 Disaster Fund | FMB News
seoDescription: The government earmarked ₱45.67 billion for the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund in the proposed 2027 budget as a fiscal buffer for El Niño and other disasters.
deck: The proposed calamity fund is 14.68% higher than the 2026 allocation and is intended to backstop regular agency resources during climate and disaster emergencies.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The government has earmarked about ₱45.67 billion for the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund under the proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program, according to the Department of Budget and Management.
Acting Budget Secretary Kim Robert de Leon said the proposed allocation is 14.68% higher than the 2026 level and is intended to provide a fiscal buffer for El Niño and other disasters.

sections.heading: How the fund would work
paragraphs: De Leon told senators that the NDRRMF can be tapped when regular agency resources are no longer enough. He cited the Department of Agriculture's existing resources for food and water security as an example of funding that would be used before the standby disaster fund covers a shortfall.

De Leon said existing Risk Resiliency Program data cover a broader range of climate and disaster risks and must be disaggregated before an amount attributable specifically to El Niño can be identified.

sections.heading: Agriculture and food security
paragraphs: DBM said the government has provided additional support for agricultural inputs, including fertilizer and fuel assistance, while the National Food Authority is using its existing budget for rice buffer stocking.
Public Works resources may also be used to repair or rehabilitate damaged rainwater collection facilities as part of preparedness measures.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The approved FMB News brief described broader disaster-preparedness initiatives, but its claims about a separate ₱1-billion Project NOAH allocation and a formal 'Super El Niño' designation were not reproduced in the primary same-day source reviewed for publication. Those details are therefore not presented here as established components of the ₱45.67-billion fund.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The proposed increase would give the government a larger standby fund when regular agency budgets are insufficient, but its practical effect will depend on congressional approval, release rules and how quickly eligible communities can access support after a disaster.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The ₱45.67-billion allocation remains part of the proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program and will be subject to congressional budget deliberations before final enactment.
